newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK pager firms said to censor anti-Beijing insults.
newsitem.headline: HK pager firms said to censor anti-Beijing insults.

text.p: Message-paging firms in Hong have censored anti-Beijing remarks that insulted Communist Party leaders ahead of the British colony's July 1 return to China, a newspaper said on Thursday.

The South China Morning Post said its survey of five pager firms found three had refused to take a message describing Chinese Premier Li Peng as a "turtle's egg", a common Chinese insult, on grounds that it was defamatory.
The expression is equivalent to calling someone in English a "bastard."
Concerns have been raised about censorship in the media and in business in Hong Kong as the 156-year-old British colony prepares to revert to China at midnight on June 30.

Beijing has pledged the territory of 6.4 million people can keep its economic and political way of life intact for 50 years, but it has already taken steps to trim back democracy and political liberties after the handover.
